transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-07
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alicia (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Jon (Redwood SE), Priya (Atlas HoML), Ethan (Platform), Sara (Security), Luis (Data Scientist)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, optional): Quick sync to lock down pass/fail criteria and artifact formats for POC acceptance. Some noise in audio; transcription medium quality.

[00:00] Alicia (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off — hopefully a short practical session, the goal is to lock the go no go thresholds and agree the reporting format so your team can sign the POC acceptance once we run benchmarks. Marcus will own the run.

[00:22] Priya (Atlas): thanks Alicia. high level — Atlas wants to validate that the model can answer regulatory queries and extract entities from policy docs. We're mostly focused on p95 latency, slot throughput and an accuracy metric (F1) for NER-ish extraction. timeline is tight; execs expect results within three weeks.

[01:10] Marcus (Redwood SE): got it. couple clarifying q's: what's your expected payload size and typical sequence length? that drives kernel selection and latency.

[01:35] Luis (Data Scientist): typical input is 800-1,200 tokens after tokenization, average closer to 900. batch of 1 in prod but we can run batched throughput tests. Also some multi-turn context for followups, but primary gating is single-turn extraction.

[02:05] Ethan (Platform): on infra constraints — we need VPC-only connectivity and KMS for keys; we can't send sensitive docs outside our approved regions. is Redwood Private in scope?

[02:28] Jon (Redwood): yes, Private is an option. for the POC we suggested Redwood hosted with customer VPC peering and envelope encryption to speed time to result; if that fails the Dedicated path is next. We'll provide KMS integration checklist.

[03:01] Sara (Security): quick pause — we need SOC 2 and ISO snapshot, retention controls, and audit logs. also data residency — all processing must happen in us-west-2.

[03:20] Alicia: noted. we'll share the SOC 2 attestation and SIEM integration notes.

[03:40] Priya: ok on security, moving to thresholds. We propose the following as initial go/no-go: p95 latency under 500ms for single-turn (900 tokens), throughput >= 30 qps sustained, NER F1 >= 0.88 on your labeled holdout, and false positive rate under 6%. if any of these fail we'd consider it a non-pass. thoughts?

[04:22] Marcus: couple of quick points — 500ms p95 for 900 tokens is aggressive but plausible on optimized inference; depends on model size and quantization. are you open to p95 within 750ms for first run and then tightening to 500ms for the final acceptance?

[04:51] Priya: we can do a two-stage threshold: mini-run pass/fail for pilot (go/no-go) and then a full-run acceptance. For pilot: p95 < 750ms, throughput >= 20 qps, F1 >= 0.85. For final POC acceptance: p95 < 500ms, throughput >= 30 qps, F1 >= 0.88.

[05:28] Luis: what's the allowable variance on the F1? we need confidence intervals.

[05:40] Jon: we'll run bootstrap sampling and provide 95% CI in the report. pass gate is mean F1 above threshold and lower CI above (threshold - 0.03) so you have statistical confidence. we'll document the exact method in the report template.

[06:12] Ethan: cost matters too. can we capture cost per million tokens and compare hosted vs dedicated runs? Execs will want unit economics.

[06:28] Alicia: yes we'll include cost-per-token estimates in the reporting. for Hosted pilot we'll give measured cost for the run; for Dedicated we'll give modeled costs.

[06:42] Sara: retention policy question — after the run, what's kept and for how long? we need to ensure ephemeral storage or retention only for debug window.

[06:55] Marcus: default retention for pilot artifacts is 7 days unless you request longer. we can configure logs to be forwarded to your S3 in us-west-2 and then purge on your schedule.

[07:10] Priya: good. now on workload sizing and test plan: we want a 48 hour mini-run that simulates production mix: 70% single-turn extraction, 20% multi-turn clarification, 10% heavy docs (8k tokens). can Redwood simulate variable seq length and traffic bursts?

[07:38] Jon: yes our harness supports variable seq length distribution and tail burst patterns. we'll provide a JMeter-style workload JSON and a harness link (redwood: https://redwood.ai/harness/poc-atlas) for you to review.

[08:02] Luis: will you run local KV-cache warmup? a cold-run will be unfair.

[08:15] Marcus: we'll do both: a cold-start pass and a warmed pass; report will separate cold/warm metrics and token-level breakup.

[08:32] Priya: reporting format — we need a one-page executive summary, detailed time-series charts (p50/p95/p99 latency), confusion matrices for extraction classes, and raw sample examples for qualitative review. also include the pass/fail matrix with every gate result.

[08:55] Alicia: agreed. we'll produce a single PDF report plus raw CSVs and a short runbook that lists configs. We'll send a sample report after the pilot.

[09:12] Ethan: on instrumentation — we want per-token billing and per-request latency traces, and traces tied to request IDs.

[09:25] Jon: Redwood tracing will expose request IDs and token billing; we'll also provide a per-request trace link for sample failing cases.

[09:38] Sara: audit logs — need immutable event logs for inference calls. can you provide a log export option that hooks into our SIEM?

[09:49] Marcus: yes, we can stream logs into your Kinesis or S3 with object-level immutability if required. we'll detail the integration steps in the security checklist.

[10:05] Priya: ok good. scoring and pass/fail mechanics: we want each gate to be boolean, and overall pass is all gates green. For any single gate fail, we get a remediation window of 5 business days to attempt a retest. does Redwood agree?

[10:26] Alicia: that's reasonable. We'll align contract language for the remediation window. We'll also capture root-cause analysis if a gate fails.

[10:40] Luis: one more on evaluation data — some of our labels have inter-annotator variance; we'll include gold labels but also human-eval on a 200-sample set. can the report include human-eval scoring?

[10:55] Jon: yes we'll run blind human eval with your team or with a third-party raters. results included as a separate section.

[11:10] Priya: timeline: we want the mini-run this week. the ask — Redwood to send the benchmark harness and we to review sample subset by Monday, run on Wednesday-Thursday, report Friday. feasible?

[11:25] Marcus: tight but doable if we get dataset subset and access by EOD Monday. I will coordinate infra and schedule.

[11:40] Alicia: so action recap — Marcus will send config and runbook, Alicia will send pricing + contract draft, Priya will share sample dataset, Sara will confirm retention/compliance details.

[11:58] Priya: on reporting delivery format — one PDF executive + CSVs + a short runbook — got it. also include a short video walkthrough of key dashboards.

[12:15] Alicia: we'll record a 10 minute walkthrough video and attach it.

[12:30] Ethan: competitor note — if we can't meet p95 < 500ms at final acceptance, we might explore cached reranking or smaller quantized models; Anthropic came up as reference but your cost numbers vs Bedrock are important.

[12:53] Marcus: yes we can test model variants and quantization levels; we'll include at least two model variants in the run so you can compare latency/quality tradeoffs.

[13:10] Sara: security final note — please anonymize logs before they land in our analytics buckets. we want clear steps for redaction.

[13:22] Jon: we'll provide a redaction script and recommend pre-ingest rules.

[13:40] Alicia: any other open items?

[13:47] Luis: wondering about success signoff doc — can you provide a one-page acceptance certificate template? execs prefer that.

[13:58] Alicia: yes, we'll attach an acceptance template as part of the report package.

[14:10] Priya: perfect. last question — if we hit all gates but cost is higher than forecast, do we have options to tune for cost (quantization, batching)?

[14:24] Marcus: absolutely. Redwood Optimize recommendations will include batching/quantization knobs and expected unit cost delta. we'll add quick recommendations in the report.

[14:40] Alicia: ok wrap up — we'll capture these as action items. look for benchmark harness link and pricing by tomorrow EOD. schedule the mini-run once dataset is approved. thanks everyone.

[14:58] Priya: thanks all.

End transcript.

References shared: Deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/poc-playbook , Harness: https://redwood.ai/harness/poc-atlas , Security checklist note: https://redwood.ai/security/snapshot

Action items (repeated in transcript): Marcus to prepare benchmark config & runbook; Priya to provide sample request templates; Alicia to send pricing & draft; Sara to confirm compliance details.

Notes about transcription quality: multiple overlapping speakers near the start; some product names transcribed as 'Redwood Private' vs 'Redwood private' inconsistently.
